newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-BICC job cuts loom after sluggish H1.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BICC job cuts loom after sluggish H1.

text.p: British cables to construction group BICC Plc warned on Wednesday of more major job cuts in its loss-making German and Italian power cable divisions which helped to depress half year profits.

But BICC said despite the difficult outlook for some of its businesses, improvements in its construction division Balfour Beatty plus efforts to tackle its cable problems meant the outlook for the second half was better.

"Overall, although we still face difficult conditions in some parts of our business, the outlook for Balfour Beatty is better and we are making progress towards solving the basic problems in power cables," said chairman Viscount Weir in a statement.
Alan Jones, chief executive, told Reuters he expected a better second half for the group as a whole.
Pretax profits for the first half moved back into the black to 55 million pounds ($86.8 million) from a two million loss after accounting for a 65 million one-off charge last year.
The underlying picture was more disappointing, with interim profits falling 13 percent after last year's charges are stripped out. BICC's half year dividend was frozen at four pence per share.
Plans for the second half will be headed by further job cuts in continental Europe, said BICC.
Jones said the power cables division in Germany would see its 700 strong workforce cut further. BICC has already reduced the headcount from 2,000 in previous job purges.
Jones told Reuters he could not comment on how many would go in Germany this time, but added an announcement would be made shortly.
"In Italy we have recently agreed a plan...to reduce our numbers employed by a further 350 people," out of a 1,230-strong workforce, Jones said.
That move should boost cost savings beyond the current 40 million pounds per annum, buttressing the year end profit line.
Jones said it was a sensible move and followed competitors who were also cutting capacity.

The European power cable market has been dogged by overcapacity and cut-throat competition as newly privatised customers in sectors like telecoms demand keener pricing from suppliers. Government spending on infrastructure has also been reduced.
BICC's first half results were undermined by the loss-making power cables business in Europe and a dull performance in Australia which outweighed the improvement at Balfour Beatty.
In a divisional breakdown, Balfour Beatty was the star performer, achieving a 15 million profit versus one million last year.

BICC Cables' profits collapsed to 28 million from 51 million, BICC Cables Corporation profits edged up one million to eight million in profit, Metal Manufactures saw profits fall to 14 million from 20 million and BICC Developments' losses were frozen at four million.
Profits from other operations were level at seven million. Group sales at BICC fell to 2.22 billion from 2.37 billion the previous year.
BICC shares were unchanged at 170 pence. ($ = 0.633 British Pounds)
